Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers, sharp problem-solvers and builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. Private markets have been closed to everyday investors for decades. The Capital Markets team is opening them. As the Product Manager for this team you will own the products that give retail investors access to companies before they reach the public markets including: 

  1. IPO Access, which distributes pre-IPO share allocations to our customers 
  2. Robinhood Ventures, our family of publicly traded funds holding direct positions in the world’s best private companies 
  3. New products you will define to give investors direct access to individual private companies and alternative investments.  

As a Senior Product Manager on Capital Markets, you will own these product lines end to end and help shape where all three go next. You’ll own the strategy and products that help everyday investors access IPOs, Private Companies, Alternatives and more. You'll work with our top tier engineers, designers, researchers, data scientists, and investing team to ship industry-changing products that revolutionize access to private markets. Today private markets are the largest category of assets ordinary investors cannot touch. This is a chance to change that.

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA or New York, NY offices, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you'll do

  • Own the strategy, roadmap, and execution for one of the Capital Markets product lines - IPO Access, Robinhood Ventures, or single-asset private offerings - and contribute to the strategy across all three
  • Lead 0-1 launches, including the in-app experience for investing in a single private asset and the discovery surfaces that make private markets navigable for a first-time investor
  • Translate ambiguous regulatory, operational, and partner requirements into clear, dependable customer experiences, working shoulder to shoulder with legal, compliance, and operations
  • Build and manage relationships with external partners - issuers, underwriters, fund administrators, and infrastructure vendors - so that a shared product actually ships
  • Set the quality bar for a product line where a confusing flow costs customers real money and real trust
  • Use research, experimentation, and product analytics to decide what to build, and to prove what worked
  • Communicate strategy, tradeoffs, and the reasoning behind them to senior leadership

What you bring

  • 5+ years of product management experience building and shipping high-quality consumer or consumer fintech products
  • A track record of shipping 0-1 products at scale, beyond prototypes and pilots
  • Comfort with financial products that carry genuine complexity - you can become an expert in a new instrument, offering structure, or regulatory regime quickly.
  • Experience working with legal, compliance, operations, or other regulated-product stakeholders, and the judgment to know when to push and when to redesign
  • Experience working with 3rd-party partners on large-scale projects to deliver a shared product
  • Strong product judgment and the ability to turn an ambiguous opportunity into a clear strategy, roadmap, and execution plan
  • Ability to operate in unclear, 0-1 situations while sustaining a high quality bar under real time pressure
  • Demonstrated history of using research, experimentation, and analytics to guide decision making
  • Clear communication and relationship management skills, with experience influencing across highly cross-functional teams and with external partners
  • Passion for Robinhood's mission to democratize finance for all, and excitement about opening an asset class that has been closed to most investors
  • Experience and proficiency building through the latest AI tools such as Claude Code, Gemini, Cursor, or ChatGPT
  • Nice to have - familiarity with private markets or alternatives - closed-end funds, BDCs, interval funds, SPVs, Reg D offerings, or the IPO / ECM process.

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career
  • Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, and equity ownership
  • Top tier benefits to fuel your work, including supplemental health insurance, ancillary insurance, and mental health support programs
  • Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible employer-paid benefits spending account expenses beyond traditional benefits such as wellness, childcare, learning, and more.
  • Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, paid volunteer time off, parental leave, and more!

descriptions.job-11rcl7i:
About Helius

Helius is building the core infrastructure for Solana - empowering developers to create the next generation of crypto-powered applications. Our mission is to accelerate the development of internet capital markets by making it easier, faster, and more intuitive to build on-chain.

Thousands of teams - from early-stage startups to industry leaders like Coinbase, Phantom, and Jupiter - rely on Helius APIs, webhooks, and indexing tools to power their products. Backed by Haun Ventures, Founders Fund, and Foundation Capital, we’re a small, senior team obsessed with performance, simplicity, and scalability in decentralized systems.

Read our Helius Manifesto to see how we work and what we value.

About the Role

This is a senior product role at Helius - you'll own product across our entire data platform: real-time streaming (LaserStream), historical and archival data, RPC infrastructure, APIs, webhooks, and developer tooling. Our customers are engineers at trading firms, wallets, and data platforms, and the product decisions that matter to them are latency budgets, delivery guarantees, and API ergonomics.

Our best engineers make product decisions, and we expect our PM to return the favor. You should write enough code to use our products the way customers do - prototype an idea, reproduce a bug, contribute when it's the fastest path to shipping. You won't ship production systems, but you should never need someone to show you what our APIs feel like to build against.

The engineering problems are hard: throughput, fan-out, ordering, historical replay. The product problems are harder to see: which guarantees to promise, what a firehose should cost, how to make a powerful primitive easy to adopt. Your job is making the platform coherent without sacrificing performance. You'll be embedded with engineering, in the room on enterprise deals, and constantly in front of customers.

What You'll Do

  • Own the product roadmap across the Helius developer platform, balancing customer requests, infrastructure investments, and new product bets

  • Spend real time with customers - trading firms, wallets, indexers - understanding their architectures, latency budgets, and where our products fit or fall short

  • Use our products hands-on and make code contributions where they're the fastest path: prototypes, example integrations, reproducing customer issues, and improving developer-facing tooling

  • Track the competitive landscape closely (streaming providers, data API vendors) and translate it into positioning, pricing, and build/kill decisions

  • Define product guarantees: delivery semantics, ordering, SLAs, and the trade-offs we're willing to make between performance, cost, and simplicity

  • Write specs and decision memos that give staff-level engineers clear context without prescribing implementation

  • Own pricing and packaging across the platform, including enterprise deals and usage-based models

  • Drive launches end-to-end: positioning, documentation, migration guides, changelogs, and developer communication - including sensitive comms like pricing changes, billing corrections, and migration notices

  • Instrument and track what matters: adoption, activation, usage growth, churn signals, latency and reliability SLOs, and revenue

  • Build the lightweight product processes a senior remote team actually needs (and kill the ones it doesn't)

What You'll Bring

  • 5+ years of product management experience on technical, developer-facing products - streaming/messaging systems, data infrastructure, APIs, market data, or similar

  • Engineering experience and working coding ability - you can write code, integrate against our APIs yourself, and prototype without waiting on an engineer. It can be minimal, but it must be real.

  • Genuine technical depth: you understand distributed systems trade-offs, can reason about throughput, backpressure, and delivery guarantees, and can hold your own with staff engineers

  • Crypto experience - you've built in, worked on, or shipped products for blockchain ecosystems and understand how on-chain data, wallets, and transactions work

  • Experience serving demanding technical customers - ideally trading firms, fintech, or other latency-sensitive users - and turning their raw feedback into prioritized product decisions

  • A track record of owning product outcomes: adoption, revenue, or retention numbers you can speak to

  • Strong pricing instincts for usage-based infrastructure products

  • Exceptional written communication - we're remote and async-heavy, and your specs and memos need to stand on their own, including customer-facing comms on sensitive topics

  • Comfort operating with high autonomy as the primary product voice in the company

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience as a software engineer, or a history of shipping meaningful code contributions as a PM

  • Direct experience with real-time market data, event streaming (Kafka, gRPC streaming, WebSockets at scale), or exchange/trading infrastructure

  • Solana-specific experience - you've built on Solana or worked deeply with its data model, RPC layer, or ecosystem

  • Experience as an early, founding, or lead PM at an infrastructure or devtools company

Why Helius?

  • High-impact work: Your code will power applications used by millions across the Solana ecosystem, including Coinbase, Jupiter, and Phantom.

  • Serious engineering: Build fast, reliable systems and user experiences across distributed infra, high-throughput backends, and modern frontend stacks.

  • Ownership & growth: Lead critical initiatives, influence architecture and product direction, and take on more responsibility as the company scales.

  • Remote-first flexibility: Work where you’re most effective with a flexible, fully distributed team.

  • Competitive comp & perks: Market-leading salary, meaningful equity, generous vacation, wellness budgets, and support for learning and travel.

  • Mission-driven team: Join ambitious builders who move fast, take ownership, and are shaping the future of decentralized apps.
descriptions.job-02z8xjy:
About Coinflow

Coinflow is the next-generation payment service provider revolutionizing global financial infrastructure with stablecoins, AI-driven fraud prevention, and instant settlement. Coinflow enables businesses to grow faster with instant settlement, fraud & chargeback indemnity, global pay-ins, multi-currency FX, and unified payouts. Founded in 2023, the company serves marketplaces, fintechs, remittance providers, gaming platforms, and ecommerce merchants worldwide.

Since our seed round in 2024, we’ve achieved 23x revenue growth and scaled to multi-billion-dollar annual transaction volume. In response to this growth, Coinflow announced a $25M Series A in October 2025—led by Pantera Capital, CMT Digital, Coinbase Ventures, Jump Crypto, and Reciprocal Ventures—accelerating our mission to power the world’s fastest-moving businesses with innovative, reliable global payments.

Coinflow is proudly headquartered in Chicago, IL. Learn more at coinflow.cash.

The Role

As a KYC Analyst, you will be responsible for overseeing the Know Your Customer (KYC) and Know Your Business (KYB) lifecycle for our merchants. This role is critical to ensuring Coinflow remains compliant while enabling smooth onboarding.. You will conduct thorough reviews and manage ongoing program requirements, while also identifying gaps and opportunities to improve our processes. You will develop SOPs, design and implement new workflows, and partner closely with Product and Engineering to drive product changes, tooling improvements, and automation. You will help protect our platform from regulatory and compliance risks, collaborating closely with internal teams across Compliance & Risk, Engineering, Integrations, Support, etc.

What You'll Do

  • KYC/KYB Reviews: Own KYC/KYB reviews throughout merchant onboarding, ensuring compliance with applicable requirements while identifying opportunities to improve review quality, efficiency, and scalability.

  • EDD Reviews: Manage Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) reviews of KYC information during merchant onboarding, knowing the escalation paths for executive or leadership review or sign-off as needed.

  • Product Expansion: Handle post-onboarding merchant requests for product or regional expansion, which may require conducting additional KYC/KYB or enhanced due diligence reviews to ensure compliance with new jurisdictional standards.

  • Periodic Reviews & Recordkeeping: Oversee ongoing KYC/KYB maintenance and periodic reviews, ensuring merchant records remain complete and current and coordinating collection of updated documentation as needed.

  • Program Management: Drive KYC/KYB initiatives as Coinflow expands into new regions, products, and banking relationships, translating new requirements into operational processes, controls, and playbooks working alongside Global MLROs and Underwriting Team.

  • Collaboration: Serve as a subject matter expert for internal stakeholders by providing guidance on KYC documentation requirements and resolving compliance-related inquiries across the organization.

  • KYC Reliance Reviews: Perform compliance assessments of partner KYC/AML programs for merchants utilizing third-party verification, ensuring alignment with Coinflow's reliance standards prior to integration.

Required Qualifications

  • 2+ years of experience in KYC/AML within fintech, payments, or banking.

  • Subject matter expertise with different jurisdictional compliance requirements and KYC/KYB for business entities and individuals.

  • Familiarity with fraud signals and the ability to detect these during KYC review.

  • Develop and manage program-level processes and requirements with a view toward growing into a team lead position.

  • Strong communication skills and comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-paced environments.

  • Bachelor's degree in Political Science/Liberal Arts, Business, Economics or a related field.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working with KYC/KYB platforms such as Persona, Middesk, Sumsub, or similar identity and business verification tools.

  • Familiarity with KYC/KYB and AML requirements across the US, Canada, EU, LATAM, or other international markets.

  • Experience in payments, fintech, banking, or another highly regulated, high-growth environment.

  • Familiarity with bank, acquirer, or payment partner compliance requirements and due diligence expectations.

  • Experience building or improving KYC/KYB workflows, SOPs, controls, and operational processes.

  • Background in high-growth payment companies and knowledge of banking partner requirements.

The base salary range for this role is $85,000 to $110,000 USD. The actual base salary offered depends on a variety of factors, including but not limited to experience, education, skills, qualifications and business needs.

In addition, the employee who fills this role will be eligible for an equity grant, allowing you to share in the long-term success of the company. You will also have access to a wide array of benefits, including health and wellness benefits, 401(k) savings plan, and flexible time off.

Join the team rewriting how money moves worldwide—and become a driving force in the $194 trillion cross-border payments market.

Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. This includes broker-dealers, investment advisors, wealth managers, hedge funds, and crypto exchanges, totalling over 10 million brokerage accounts.

Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it.

Alpaca is proudly backed by $400 million in funding from top-tier global investors including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Opera Tech Ventures, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Unbound, Peak XV, Elefund, and Y Combinator.

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Role

Lead the team that commands Alpaca's most critical incidents. You will build the function and then keep raising its bar: the severity model, the escalation and communication paths, 24x7 follow-the-sun coverage, and the KPIs that prove it is improving. You will do that across boundaries - with the engineering teams who own the services, with SRE on reliability standards and on-call readiness, with Risk on financial and regulatory materiality, with our partner communications teams on what reaches a customer, and with reliability programme management on what happens after.

You will own how well we respond. Not the fix, not the partner communication, and not the reliability standard. Holding that line is a deliberate part of the design and a core part of the job.

Things You Get To Do

  • Build the team and stand up 24x7 command. Recruit and certify Incident Commanders, build a follow-the-sun rotation across APAC, EMEA and AMER with warm handoffs at every regional boundary, and carry a rostered slot yourself. Keep the team sharp between real incidents with game days, tabletop exercises and simulations, and coach them through the live ones. Build a blameless review culture that treats an outlier as a process gap rather than a person's failure.
  • Own the process, and keep raising it. Drive severity maturity with Risk on financial and regulatory materiality - in a regulated brokerage a severity call can also start a reporting clock, so the model has to map cleanly onto those thresholds. Own the escalation path and what happens when a page goes unanswered, agree the thresholds for taking an incident to engineering leadership, and keep the service catalogue and its ownership current - time spent working out who owns a failing service is customer impact.
  • Own both bridges. Your team connects the engineers and technical support fixing the problem, who need uninterrupted focus, to the partner communications teams, who need a continuous and accurate feed. You open the channel, supply the facts and hold the update cadence to account. Afterwards, your team runs the retrospective with SRE - who own the technical depth - and builds the post-incident package while the room is still warm, every item ticketed, owned and tagged, delivered inside a service level you define and then hold, before reliability programme management drives it to closure. You then synthesise the discussion into short, digestible learnings and publish them to the whole engineering organisation, so one team's failure becomes everyone's lesson instead of a document three people read.
  • Own the KPIs. Time to respond and time to mitigate end to end, including the definitions and data hygiene beneath them: what separates mitigated from resolved, and whether a timestamp means what it claims. Establish a defensible baseline before committing to targets, then move them by severity. Review and approval, not authorship, is where postmortems stall, so report overdue reviews by team and incident with a next action against each.
  • Build it as a product, then automate it with AI. Everything is documented, versioned and deployable, so you can stand up command from the artefacts alone; the process needs to scale considerably faster than the team. The automation we are after is AI workflows and agents rather than scripts and dashboards - agents that set an incident up, assemble the timeline as it runs, draft the RCA and the action package, and chase the update that is due or the review that is overdue. You own that roadmap: what an agent may do unsupervised, what still needs a commander's judgement, and the decision-tree quality that makes either of them safe.

Who You Are (Must-Haves)

  • You have stood up an incident command or major-incident function, not only worked inside one - you have owned the severity model, built the roster and driven adoption across teams.
  • 5+ years in production engineering, SRE or technical operations, including hands-on command of high-severity incidents.
  • You have led a distributed team across time zones and run a 24x7 rotation.
  • You get engineers you do not manage to do things, and you can defend a severity call to someone who disagrees with it.
  • You have built reliability metrics people trust, and you know the difference between improving a number and improving reality.
  • You are disciplined about scope. You can say "that is not ours" and route it, in the middle of an outage, without leaving a gap.
  • You write well enough that your process documents actually get used, you can hold a bridge calm under pressure, and you can brief an executive mid-incident without either downplaying it or dramatising it.
  • You understand FinTech and the trust stakes of API-driven financial platforms.
  • You use AI and agentic automation to remove toil rather than to add tooling.

Who You Might Be (Nice-to-Haves)

  • Formal incident command training - ITIL, Major Incident Management or crisis management.
  • You have run a certification, game day or drill programme, or built a pool of certified responders beyond your own headcount.
  • Experience with modern incident management and on-call platforms.
  • You have built a service catalogue or ownership registry that people actually maintained.
  • You have worked with programme management or reliability functions to convert incident follow-ups into funded roadmap work.
  • Familiarity with incident reporting obligations in regulated financial services - DORA, Reg SCI, FINRA or equivalent.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Principal, Technology provides day-to-day operating support to the technology leader and five functional domains: Software Engineering, Data Science, IT, Networking, and Cybersecurity.

This role turns organizational priorities into coordinated execution. The principal manages intake, triages requests, drives meeting sprints and progress tracking, supports governance and audit activities, improves operating processes, and gives leadership a clear view of outcomes, active work, near-term plans, and decisions needed.

This is a hands-on role for an experienced technology project or program professional who can move comfortably between operational detail and executive-level priorities. The successful candidate will help create one coordinated technology organization while preserving the accountability and expertise of each domain.

What You'll Do

  • Serve as the day-to-day operational support to the technology leader, helping translate priorities and decisions into clear actions, owners, and follow-through.
  • Manage a single intake process across the technology organization, triaging requests, routing work to the appropriate domain lead, and escalating unclear or cross-functional items for review.
  • Prepare and coordinate leadership projects, agendas, decisions, action items, and follow-ups for due diligence and prioritization.
  • Maintain visibility into cross-functional initiatives, dependencies, risks, and blocked work, acting as a proactive escalation point when delivery begins to slip.
  • Coordinate a consistent weekly reporting cadence across the five domains, including outcomes achieved, active work, near-term plans, risks, and decisions needed.
  • Support quarterly roadmap and portfolio planning by organizing inputs, applying shared prioritization criteria, and preparing recommendations for leadership decisions.
  • Support technology governance, audit, compliance, and control activities by coordinating evidence, owners, deadlines, and executive responses.
  • Identify recurring friction in how work is requested, prioritized, planned, communicated, and delivered, then help implement practical process improvements.
  • Act as an on-demand proxy into a specific domain or issue when additional coordination, investigation, or follow-through is needed.
  • Partner with the team to improve shared templates, tools, operating rhythms, and management practices over time.
  • Help coordinate communications across the technology organization so teams understand priorities, decisions, changes, and expectations, as well as the wider organization.

ABOUT YOU

  • 5+ years of experience in technology project management, technical program management, business analysis, operations, or a similar role.

  • Demonstrated experience coordinating work across multiple teams, functions, or technical stakeholders.
  • Strong understanding of project and portfolio management fundamentals, including scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions, and ownership.
  • Technical literacy sufficient to work conversationally with engineering, data, infrastructure, networking, and cybersecurity teams. The ability to understand concepts such as APIs, systems integrations, networks, cloud services, and security controls is required; deep hands-on engineering expertise is not.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate operational detail into concise executive-level updates.
  • Excellent organization, prioritization, scheduling, meeting facilitation, and follow-through skills.
  • Sound judgment and practical instincts around escalation, missed commitments, ambiguous ownership, and slipping work.
  • Comfort operating in an evolving organization where priorities, responsibilities, and processes are still being defined.
  • Experience supporting governance, audit, compliance, or other deadline-driven control activities is preferred.
  • Experience in a technology organization is preferred. Experience limited to a non-technical business function may require significant ramp-up.

Working Style

The right person is proactive, practical, and comfortable being the connective tissue across teams. They do not wait for perfect information or formal direction to identify a gap, clarify ownership, and move work forward. They can challenge constructively, communicate directly, protect priorities, and build trust with both technical specialists and business leaders.

This role is not intended to replace the functional leads or become a centralized project-management bench. Its purpose is to provide operating leverage to the technology leader, coordinate work that crosses domains, and help the organization develop stronger distributed ownership over time.

ABOUT THE WORK ENVIRONMENT

This role is in office at our corporate headquarters in the Brickell area of Miami, Florida. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The workload is analogous to a game engine’s replay and simulation loop, a telco’s real-time packet pipeline, or a bigtech streaming and analytics platform, applied to financial market data. Domain expertise in trading and market microstructure is welcome but not required on day one; we invest heavily in onboarding and pair every new engineer with a mentor.

The stack: modern C++ for the throughput-critical ingest and simulation core, Python plus C++ bindings for research tooling, distributed compute across HPC (Slurm today, evolving). You will help deliver high-quality data, fast and flexible compute tooling, robust simulation and deployment systems, and ergonomics that let researchers iterate quickly. Work spans raw exchange data ingestion, distributed HPC orchestration, and research tooling.

Key responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain high-performance, scalable software and data systems used by quant researchers and trading teams.

  • Orchestrate and improve reliability of data and compute pipelines on HPC clusters.
  • Create ad-hoc computation frameworks and research tooling that let researchers slice, backtest, and iterate rapidly (Python + C++ integrations).
  • Develop and maintain simulation frameworks tightly integrated with HFT/live trading platforms.
  • Support training and deployment of quantitative models used in trading.
  • Monitor, manage, and troubleshoot distributed platforms.
  • Optimize codebases for performance, reliability, and resource efficiency across the full stack.

Required qualifications

  • 2+ years of professional experience building large-scale, high-performance systems; daily use of modern C++ (>=17) and Python expected.
  • Strong CS fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, networking, OS, concurrency, and system design.
  • Data engineering fluency: designing schemas, choosing storage formats, understanding compression and I/O trade-offs, and operating pipelines that write and read hundreds of TB. Comfortable reasoning about columnar formats (Parquet / Arrow) or their equivalents in your domain (event logs, telemetry, replays).
  • Experience designing and operating services or platforms used by other technical users in data-intensive environments.
  • Comfortable supporting internal users and iterating on ergonomics and workflows.
  • Demonstrated ability to ship production software safely and repeatedly, with an obsession for data driven quality.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication; collaborative mindset and empathy

Desirable / nice-to-have

  • Rust experience alongside C++ and Python.
  • Experience running compute at cluster scale: job scheduling, resource management, retries, and reliability. Slurm, Kubernetes, Ray, Spark, or custom internal schedulers all count.
  • GPU programming experience.
  • Familiarity with ML/Deep Learning frameworks.
  • Prior finance or market-data experience, including low-level market connectivity.
  • Historical network / packet processing (telco, network appliances, packet-capture replay infrastructure) - any exposure.
  • Deterministic simulation and replay systems (game engines, cell simulators, distributed-systems testing frameworks) - any exposure.

We evaluate CS fundamentals, ability to reason about correctness and performance under real constraints, code quality, communication, and clear signs of growth (asks good questions, learns fast, takes feedback well). descriptions.job-1sghrvi:
The Role

We are hiring a Product Marketing Lead to own product marketing for our Risk Applications and Enabling Services portfolio, the products our customers depend on for AML screening, transaction monitoring, payment screening, fraud detection, case management, and regulatory reporting. This is the largest and most active half of our product portfolio, with new products and features shipping continuously. You'll take ownership of each product wherever it is in its lifecycle.

You will report to the VP of Product Marketing and be one of two Product Marketing Leads building out a newly-forming function. This is a foundational hire, with real latitude to shape how product marketing operates at ComplyAdvantage. You will partner closely with the Product Director who owns this portfolio, translating a steady stream of product and feature launches into positioning, enablement and go-to-market execution that Sales and Customer Success actually use.

We run a structured, phased launch process that's still evolving and you'll help shape it as you go, deciding what's genuinely differentiated and worth a moment, and what ships quietly as a release note.

This role has no direct reports today. It is a hands-on, individual-contributor role for someone who wants to own outcomes end to end rather than manage other people's output; someone who can take ambiguous input from Product and Sales and turn it into sharp positioning and a launch that lands, without needing a team underneath them to get there.

What You Will Do

Own product marketing for Risk Applications & Enabling Services. You are responsible for positioning, messaging, launch execution and enablement for this portfolio, end to end, from early roadmap conversations through GA and beyond.

Take ownership of products at every stage. Some products in this portfolio are newly launched or launching soon; you'll pick up their ongoing positioning, enablement and buyer narrative rather than starting from a blank page, and build out what's missing.

Lead launches end to end. Decide what earns a flagship moment versus what ships quietly, and own the launch plan, messaging and positioning brief for the releases that matter most.

Build the enablement Sales actually uses. Sales decks, demos, battlecards and FAQs written from a real understanding of the buyer and competitive landscape, not templated from a brief.

Contribute to competitive intelligence and win-loss. This is shared across the Product Marketing team for now; you'll help build the muscle until we have dedicated coverage.

Represent UK/EMEA (and APAC in the interim) market context. You're the voice of our primary market in company positioning, even as we build out dedicated regional coverage over time.

Partner with Product without owning their roadmap. You influence priorities through evidence, buyer feedback, competitive dynamics, win-loss signal, not through authority. You operate as a peer to a Product Director, not a downstream recipient of their decisions.

Use AI in your own work. We expect Product Marketing to use AI-assisted workflows for research synthesis, competitive analysis, and first-draft positioning and content. This is how we work, not an aspiration.

What We Are Looking For

Essential:

  • 7-10 years of overall professional experience, including 3-5+ years in product marketing
  • Experience at a high-growth, multi-product technology company; you understand what it means to market a portfolio, not a single product, and to prioritize across competing launches
  • Demonstrated ability to own a launch end to end: positioning, sales enablement, messaging and go-to-market, without heavy oversight
  • Strong independence and autonomy: comfortable defining your own plan within a broader strategy rather than waiting for detailed direction
  • Proven ability to influence without authority: you can shape a Product Director's or sales leader's thinking through evidence and argument, not reporting lines
  • Excellent written and verbal communication: able to translate complex, technical product capability into a sharp, buyer-relevant narrative
  • Comfort operating in a regulated, technical B2B environment, translating product and engineering input into content a commercial audience can act on
  • Demonstrable AI adoption in your own working practice; already using it to work differently, not just interested in it

Preferred:

  • Experience in fintech, security, or identity markets
  • Experience marketing AI or agentic tools, platforms, or features
  • Experience marketing to multiple distinct buyer personas within the same portfolio
  • Familiarity with win-loss and competitive intelligence practices
  • Experience partnering with Sales on enterprise or upmarket motions

What Success Looks Like

At 60 days: You understand the Risk Applications and Enabling Services portfolio end to end, including any products that have recently launched or are approaching launch, and where our competitive and buyer knowledge has gaps. You've built working relationships with the Product Director for this portfolio, Sales leadership and Customer Success, and can articulate what's differentiated in our portfolio and why it matters to a buyer.

At 4 months: You are running launches independently through the tiered model. Your highest-priority products have positioning and a sales narrative that Sales trusts and uses, and your enablement materials are the ones reps actually reach for. You've built a first cut of the win-loss picture for your portfolio and can speak to it with data, not anecdote.

At 8 months: Your portfolio's go-to-market motion is measurably working; Sales can point to deals your positioning and enablement helped win. You're a trusted, senior voice in cross-functional planning for this portfolio, and you're operating at a level that could reasonably take on more scope as the team grows.

What’s in it for you?

  • Equity participation in our innovative mission to combat financial crimeUnlimited Time Off Policy to promote work-life balance and well-being
  • We embrace a hybrid approach that requires employees to be in the office for two days a week. We strongly believe that this approach fosters collaboration and enables the building of meaningful relationships
  • Opportunities for collaboration and career development with smart, like-minded professionals
  • Annual learning budget to support professional growth
  • A home office budget to support working from home
  • Enhanced parental leave and childcare benefits
  • Life insurance and medical coverage through BUPA, including pre-existing conditions
  • Pension contribution through The People's Pension

About us

Our mission is to empower every business to eliminate financial crime. 

By harnessing AI, a unified platform, and an extensive partner ecosystem, we help customers turn compliance into a catalyst for growth, operational resilience, and enduring regulatory trust.

More than 3,000 enterprises across 75 countries rely on our end-to-end platform and the world’s most comprehensive financial crime risk intelligence. With full-stack agentic automation, we help organizations automate up to 95% of KYC, AML, and sanctions reviews, cut onboarding times by 50%, reduce false positives by 70%, and handle 7x more work with the same staff.

ComplyAdvantage is headquartered in London and has global hubs in New York, Lisbon, Singapore, and Cluj-Napoca. It is backed by Balderton Capital, Index Ventures, Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, Goldman Sachs, and Andreessen Horowitz. Learn more about compliance re-engineered for the age of AI at complyadvantage.com.

  • Data & Experimentation: Track D1/D7/D30 retention, FTD conversion, repeat rate, and Net LTV; run independent analysis with AI; validate strategies and mechanisms through A/B testing.

Requirements

  • 3+ years in growth or product operations, with quantifiable growth results;
  • Deep understanding of the user lifecycle and growth funnel, with the ability to design scalable operating mechanisms;
  • Strong data-driven decision making, with a track record of shipping into production;
  • Fluent English; able to drive execution in a global team environment;
  • Hands-on data analysis and A/B testing experience; clear reasoning and strong execution;

Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.

descriptions.job-1gqv9em:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Brand Studio sits at the center of everything Stripe shows the world — from visual identity and brand systems to campaigns, events, digital experiences, and global marketing. The studio functions as a creative multiplier: setting the standards, building the systems, and producing the work that helps Stripe show up with intention and quality across every touchpoint.

World-class creative output requires world-class operational infrastructure. Brand Operations is the function that makes Brand Studio's work possible at scale — not by managing the execution, but by architecting the conditions that enable it. That means shaping what enters the studio, ensuring clarity before a brief is written, and building the systems that allow creative directors and producers to focus on what they're here to do: create exceptional work.

What you’ll do

Most operations leaders are brought in to fix problems. We're looking for someone who prevents them — and designs the system in which prevention becomes the norm.

The Head of Brand Operations exists upstream from creative execution. This role's job is to ensure the work entering Brand Studio is strategically aligned, clarified, prioritized, resourced, and fully prepared for delivery before it ever reaches a creative director or producer. It also means ensuring the company understands how to work with Brand Studio — what it takes to be a ready partner, and where a given initiative stands on the roadmap. When that infrastructure is working, creative leaders spend their time and energy on the thing they're actually here to do.

This role lives at the altitude of setting the team up for success. That means the early-stage, ambiguous conversations where partners are still forming ideas — where the business need hasn't been articulated, where the biggest risks and opportunities haven't been named, and where a structural decision will compound over time. It means building and maintaining a roadmap the entire company can see and trust. And it means leading a team of producers who own their projects fully, with your role being the system that makes their ownership meaningful.

This role isn't about staying out of the details entirely — it's about not defaulting to them. You'll roll up your sleeves when the moment calls for it. But your primary value is in designing the ecosystem, not running the work. If you want to build the system in which great work consistently becomes possible — and watch it scale — this is a rare opportunity to do that.

Responsibilities

  •  Architect the Brand Studio ecosystem. Engage cross-functional partners — Marketing, Product, Comms, PMM — before briefs exist. Turn ambiguous asks into clear, sequenced workstreams so creative leaders inherit clarity, not chaos.
  • Build and maintain the Brand Studio roadmap. Sequence and prioritize work based on business importance, creative opportunity, and team capacity. Give leadership a forward-looking view of what's coming — and the tradeoffs involved.
  • Set the conditions for great work. By the time a project reaches a creative director or producer, the business need is defined, stakeholders are aligned, and the problem is framed. Creative leaders shape the work. You shape the environment that makes the work possible.
  • Own and evolve the operational infrastructure. Build the intake processes, alignment frameworks, and communication rhythms that help Brand Studio run at scale. Refine them as the team grows.
  • Make how Brand Studio works visible to the company. Partners should be able to find the roadmap, understand where their project stands, and know what it takes to show up ready. The process of working with Brand Studio shouldn't require a meeting to explain.
  • Run the business of Brand Studio. Own the budget, manage agency and external production partnerships from procurement through delivery standards, and partner with Finance on clear accounting structures. Give the team the resources and partnerships it needs to deliver.
  • Lead, develop, and set the cultural tone. Hire great people, build their judgment, and set clear ownership. Give direct feedback, delegate fully, and create the stability that lets people do their best work. You're a steward of how this team shows up — the norms, the standards, and what it means to operate at this level.
  • Stay attuned to what's forming. Brand-level initiatives take shape before briefs exist. Catch early signals across the company and help shape ambiguous ideas into clear outcomes before they reach the studio.
  • Represent Brand Studio at the leadership level. Keep senior leaders informed on priorities, direction, and impact. Make the case for what deserves investment, what should wait, and why.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 12+ years of experience in brand operations, creative operations, or creative program management. A track record of building operational systems at the function level, not just executing inside them.
  • 5+ years managing a team of producers, program managers, or operations professionals, with clear evidence of developing talent and building production capability.

What is Kalshi?

Kalshi has defined a new category: prediction markets. Kalshi allows people to trade on the outcome of any events and turn any question about the future into a financial asset. Kalshi fought for years and legalized prediction markets in the US for the first time in history, is currently the fastest growing financial market in America, and has thousands of markets across politics, economics, financials, weather, tech, AI, culture and more.

We believe prediction markets have the potential to be the largest financial market because they turn anything into a financial position.

  • Our vision: well… build the largest financial market on the planet.

Our culture is simple: we hire really talented people, work really hard, and enjoy the climb. We are looking for ambitious and exceptional people to join our (relatively small) team to help us build the next generation of financial markets.

Role Roadmap

As a Recruiter at Kalshi, you'll own full-cycle recruiting across the entire company - from engineering and product to compliance, operations, and go-to-market. You'll partner directly with hiring managers and leadership to define what great looks like for a role, go find it, and close it. There's almost no red tape here: no drawn-out approval chains, no bureaucracy standing between you and a great candidate. It’s the right role for you if you’re incredibly self-directed, you move fast, take ownership over your pipelines, and can attract → close the best talent in the world.

 

What You'll Do

  • Own full-cycle recruiting for a mix of technical and non-technical roles, from intake through offer and close

  • Partner directly with hiring managers and leadership to build role scorecards, sharpen hiring criteria, and design efficient interview processes

  • Proactively source and engage passive candidates across channels, building strong outbound pipelines rather than waiting on inbound

  • Manage a high-volume, fast-moving pipeline while maintaining a high bar and a great candidate experience

  • Act as a trusted advisor to hiring managers on market data, leveling, and competitive offers

  • Represent Kalshi's mission and culture compellingly to candidates at every stage

 

What You Bring

  • Proven ability to build strong outbound pipelines and close passive candidates, not just manage inbound flow

  • Comfort operating across very different hiring profiles - from engineers to operators to compliance and gtm hires - without losing quality or speed

  • Strong judgment and the ability to move fast and make decisions autonomously in a low-process environment

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, especially with senior hiring managers

About the Company

Gemini is a global crypto and Web3 platform founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2014, offering a wide range of simple, reliable, and secure crypto products and services to individuals and institutions in over 70 countries. Our mission is to unlock the next era of financial, creative, and personal freedom by providing trusted access to the decentralized future. We envision a world where crypto reshapes the global financial system, internet, and money to create greater choice, independence, and opportunity for all — bridging traditional finance with the emerging cryptoeconomy in a way that is more open, fair, and secure. As a publicly traded company, Gemini is poised to accelerate this vision with greater scale, reach, and impact.

The Department: Platform

Our Platform organization’s purpose is to enable Gemini to scale effectively and empower our engineering teams to focus on building innovative financial products and experiences for individuals around the world. Platform focuses on building a scalable and secure foundations platform, enabling Engineering to develop, deploy, validate, and operate services in production; improve resiliency; increase organizational efficiency by reducing operational toil; and improve system efficiency through architectural evolution.

The Platform team builds products for engineers. We work directly with product, data, security, and infrastructure teams to understand their needs, establish safe and opinionated defaults, and provide paved paths that make the reliable choice the easy choice. We treat internal platforms as production software with users, service-level objectives, roadmaps, documentation, and feedback loops, not as collections of configuration.

The Role: Senior Platform Engineer

You will design, build, and operate the software and infrastructure that form Gemini’s internal engineering platform. This is a software engineering role grounded in deep production and infrastructure experience. You will build self-service systems, developer tools, and automation that improve the way teams create, deploy, scale, observe, and operate services.

You will partner with engineering teams to turn broad operational needs into reliable platform products. You will make infrastructure programmable, secure, observable, and resilient; use SLOs and error budgets to guide tradeoffs; and continuously replace manual operational work with well-designed software. The role spans software, systems, and infrastructure engineering, with an emphasis on durable abstractions and measurable improvements to developer velocity and production reliability.

The role spans cloud platforms, networking, compute, storage, infrastructure automation, CI/CD, and the systems required to run highly available services in production.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain platform services, APIs, CLIs, controllers, and automation in languages such as Go, Python, or similar; own them through design, implementation, testing, deployment, and production operation.
  • Build self-service capabilities that let engineers provision environments, deploy services, manage infrastructure, and respond to operational conditions safely without relying on manual platform intervention.
  • Create and evolve paved paths for service development and delivery, including templates, libraries, deployment workflows, policy-as-code, and reusable platform primitives.
  • Design and improve the cloud, compute, storage, identity, and infrastructure primitives used by engineering teams.
  • Design and operate core network infrastructure — VPCs, Cloud Routing, and security controls across public clouds and regions. 
  • Operate and improve the compute, container, networking, and cloud foundations that support critical services and emerging workloads, including distributed and AI-enabled systems where appropriate.
  • Improve the systems and workflows used to provision infrastructure, connect services, deliver changes, and recover from failures across environments.
  • Define and use service-level indicators, SLOs, error budgets, and production-readiness standards to make reliability and launch decisions explicit and measurable.
  • Improve observability, alerting, capacity planning, performance, and failure handling; design systems that degrade gracefully, roll out progressively, and recover automatically where safe.
  • Participate in an appropriately staffed on-call rotation, lead incident response when needed, and turn incidents and recurring operational work into permanent improvements through blameless postmortems and follow-through.
  • Reduce toil deliberately. Measure repetitive operational work, automate or eliminate it, and keep the team focused primarily on engineering work that improves reliability, scale, security, cost, or developer experience.
  • Collaborate with product and engineering teams on architecture, productionization, and technical design; provide guidance without becoming a ticket-based operations layer.
  • Establish technical direction through design documents, prototypes, testing, metrics, and iterative delivery. Make pragmatic tradeoffs while preserving clear interfaces and room for future evolution.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering, infrastructure engineering, SRE, or an equivalent combination of experience, including meaningful ownership of production systems.
  • Strong software engineering ability in at least one language such as Go, Python, Java, Rust, or similar, with experience building maintainable services, automation, CLIs, APIs, or developer tools - not only scripts or one-off configuration.
  • Demonstrated experience operating infrastructure and distributed systems in production, including diagnosing failures, managing capacity, improving performance, and designing for high availability and recovery.
  • Experience designing, operating, or improving production systems across cloud infrastructure, networking, compute, storage, deployment platforms, or related infrastructure domains.
  • Hands-on experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure and infrastructure as code, such as Terraform or an equivalent system.
  • Experience with containers and orchestration, such as Kubernetes, EKS, GKE, Docker, or Nomad, including workload deployment, networking, security, and operational troubleshooting.
  • Experience owning and managing cloud network security controls, including network firewalls, DNS filtering, and network segmentation.
  • Experience designing or improving CI/CD and automated software delivery systems, including testing, deployment, progressive rollout, rollback, and change validation.
  • Practical experience with observability: metrics, logs, traces, alerting, dashboards, and production health models. Familiarity with OpenTelemetry or comparable tooling is valuable.
  • Working knowledge of SLOs, error budgets, incident response, blameless postmortems, and techniques for reducing operational toil.

About the role

We turn raw on-chain activity into trustworthy intelligence — clustering addresses into real-world entities, attributing them to services and actors, and surfacing risk for compliance and investigations teams. We're looking for a data scientist who is as comfortable shipping a heuristic to production as they are designing it: someone who can move from a messy hypothesis to a working pipeline without waiting on someone else to wire up the data.

You'll work closely with our attribution and clustering leads on models and heuristics that run across billions of transactions and multiple chains (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Solana, and more).

What you'll do

  • Design, test, and ship clustering and attribution heuristics, and measure them with real precision/coverage metrics rather than vibes.

  • Own your data end to end — pull, clean, join, and model large on-chain datasets without depending on a separate team for every query.

  • Build and maintain the pipelines that take a heuristic from notebook to production, including backfills, incremental runs, and validation.

  • Investigate edge cases (mixers, bridges, exchange hot wallets, consolidation patterns) and translate findings into repeatable logic.

  • Partner with investigations and product to define what "correct" looks like and benchmark against ground truth.

  • Prototype quickly, then harden what works.

What we're looking for

  • 4+ years building data science or data engineering systems that actually shipped (not just notebooks).

  • Strong Python and SQL; comfortable with large datasets and the gotchas of joins, dedup, and skew at scale.

  • Solid grasp of clustering, graph/network analysis, or entity resolution — and a habit of validating results, not just producing them.

  • Ability to reason about precision vs. coverage trade-offs and defend your metrics.

  • Self-directed: you can scope an ambiguous problem, get the data yourself, and drive it to a result.

Our tech stack

You don't need to have used all of these, but here's what you'd be working with day to day:

  • Databricks — our lakehouse and processing backbone. Large-scale on-chain datasets are transformed and modeled here via Spark and SQL; most heuristics run as Databricks jobs against billions of transactions.

  • Kafka — real-time ingestion of on-chain and transaction data. New blocks and events stream in continuously, so a lot of our work is designed to run incrementally rather than as one-off batch jobs.

  • Python — the primary language for everything from exploratory analysis to production heuristics and pipeline code.

  • TigerGraph — our graph database, where addresses, transactions, and entities live as a network. Clustering, traversals, and relationship queries (who funds whom, consolidation paths, entity linkage) happen here.

Supporting cast you'll likely touch:

  • SQL everywhere — for ad-hoc analysis, validation, and defining ground-truth datasets.

  • Columnar / analytical stores (e.g., ClickHouse) for fast aggregate queries over large tables.

  • Orchestration & scheduling for backfills and recurring pipeline runs.

  • Git / GitHub for version control and code review — we expect pipelines and heuristics to be reviewed like any other code.

  • GCP as our cloud environment.

Small, high-trust team. You'll have a lot of ownership and very little bureaucracy. We prototype fast, measure honestly, and ship.

We care about your well-being. Along with excellent health insurance, we offer flexible time off, learning & development initiatives and hours that are designed to provide work/life balance.  We regularly host team-building sessions and encourage discussions around mental health.  

We reward talent and believe in acknowledging people for their contributions.  We offer industry-leading compensation, along with generous equity.  As a rapidly growing business, there are endless opportunities to grow your career with Merkle Science.

  • A strong portfolio demonstrating exceptional visual craft, systems thinking, and the ability to lead complex, multi-faceted design work independently

Money is moving onto the internet, and the shift has a name: Open Money. This is money that is open, portable, agentic, and owned by you. MetaMask spent the last ten years building it; with 100M+ downloads, users in ~190 countries, and trillions in cumulative transaction volume, it's the most trusted self-custodial financial platform on the internet. Now we're building the operating system for your money: one place to hold, move, grow, and use anything you own.  Join a remote-first, global team rebuilding how money works: a problem that touches everyone, every day.

About MetaMask

MetaMask is building a future where users can unlock the full product stack through a single, seamless identity experience, enabling access to all features with trust, safety, and minimal friction.

Today, identity verification is fragmented across several product and onboarding experiences. Users are repeatedly asked to verify themselves across different services, creating unnecessary friction, inconsistent outcomes, and degraded trust.

Universal KYC (UKYC) is a new initiative to solve this problem by creating a single, reusable identity layer across MetaMask. At the centre of this is MetaMask Passport, a product designed to enable users to verify once and unlock multiple experiences across the MetaMask ecosystem.

This role sits at the intersection of platform and product experience. You will define the primitives, standards, and user journeys that make identity verification seamless, privacy-conscious, and globally compliant.

What you’ll do

You will own the vision and roadmap for Universal KYC and MetaMask Passport, defining how a reusable identity layer unlocks the broader MetaMask product stack. You will build the underlying identity platform, creating scalable verification primitives and standards that can be adopted across products. In parallel, you will design a seamless, low-friction KYC experience that reduces time-to-first-transaction while maintaining compliance integrity. You will drive adoption across MetaMask by partnering closely with internal teams to integrate a consistent identity layer, while balancing privacy, trust, and global regulatory requirements. Throughout, you will lead execution end-to-end, aligning cross-functional teams and delivering measurable outcomes.

What we are looking for:

  • Proven experience building or scaling identity verification (IDV), KYC, or onboarding products
  • Strong background in fintech, ideally with exposure to Web3
  • Hands-on experience working with identity verification providers (IDV vendors) such as Sumsub, Veriff, Onfido, Persona, or Stripe Identity
  • Familiarity with compliance workflows, including KYC, KYB, and customer due diligence (CDD) processes
  • Track record of delivering platform products adopted across multiple teams
  • Ability to operate across both technical systems and user experience

What Success looks like:

  • Increased KYC completion rates and reduced onboarding friction
  • Reduced time-to-first-transaction across KYC-gated flows
  • Increased reuse of verified identity across products
  • Improved transaction success rate through consistent verification outcomes
  • Strong user trust with minimal friction and compliant execution

Attributes that will make you stand out

  • First-principles thinker with strong product judgment
  • Deep user empathy with a focus on reducing friction and cognitive load
  • Strong understanding of trust, privacy, and compliance trade-offs
  • Clear, structured communicator who drives alignment and momentum
  • High ownership and ability to operate in ambiguity

Why This Role Matters

Universal KYC is a foundational unlock for MetaMask, enabling users to move from fragmented, repetitive identity verification to a seamless, reusable experience across the entire product stack. It establishes a scalable, privacy-conscious identity layer that strengthens user trust while meeting global compliance requirements. This is a high-leverage role at the intersection of access, trust, and growth, critical to unlocking the next phase of MetaMask’s evolution.

Don't meet all the requirements? Don't sweat it. We’re passionate about building a diverse team of humans and as such, if you think you've got what it takes for our chaotic-but-fun, remote-friendly, start-up environment—apply anyway, detailing your relevant transferable skills in your cover letter. While we have a pretty good idea of what we need, we're ready for you to challenge our thinking on who needs to be in this role.

$130,000—$187,000 USD

The 4 biggest blockchain strengths are also its weakness

  • Permissionless nature leads to fragmentation of meaning

  • Decentralization leads to too many standards

  • Immutability leads to exponential data + query infrastructure complexity

  • Neutrality means that no one is accountable for interpretations

Blockchain data is public. It is not usable at institutional scale. Despite being open, blockchain data is fragmented, hard to interpret, and painful to maintain. Even a simple question like “Who are the largest Ethereum token holders over time?” can require running nodes, ingesting full chain history, decoding contracts, cleaning edge cases, and writing complex SQL.

Blockchains are optimized for writes, not reads.

They are built for consensus and execution, not searchability, standardization, or financial interpretation. Blockchains are computers, not databases. Every protocol defines its own schema. The same economic action can be encoded in dozens of different ways. The result:

  • Fragmented standards

  • Exponential complexity

  • No accountability for interpretation

  • Events without economic meaning

Finance cannot operate on that, it needs an effective system of record.

Allium is building the System of Record for Onchain Finance

Allium ingests, verifies, and standardizes data across 140+ blockchains and 30+ petabytes of history. We close four structural gaps that prevent blockchains from becoming systems of record:

  • Semantic Gap: Translating raw events into financial concepts like payments, trades, deposits, and staking income

  • Standardization Gap: Mapping thousands of protocols into a single canonical cross chain schema

  • Infrastructure Gap: Read optimized, globally distributed data at web scale

  • Accountability Gap: Auditable methodology, SLAs, and SOC 1 and 2 compliance

The result is a neutral, canonical data layer institutions can build on with confidence.

Finance is moving onchain

Stablecoins, tokenized assets, trading, staking, and lending are growing rapidly. Institutions need a trusted source of truth for onchain financial activity, just as they rely on Bloomberg or DTCC in traditional markets. Raw blockchains cannot serve that role.

As AI agents begin transacting autonomously, the requirement becomes even stricter. Agents cannot reason over raw event logs. They need structured data, attribution, condition checks, and auditability.

Allium is the read layer that makes onchain finance usable for humans and machines.

Who We Serve

Allium powers three core personas with the same canonical data foundation:

1. Finance, Accounting, and Risk Teams They need reliable, audit grade answers. They rely on Allium for financial reporting, reconciliation, compliance, risk monitoring, and defensible metrics that can stand up to auditors and regulators.

2. Engineers and Product Teams They need low latency, production ready infrastructure. They use Allium to power wallets, trading systems, payment rails, staking infrastructure, and real time applications that cannot break.

3. Strategy, Research, and Executive Teams They need clarity and insight. They use Allium to understand ecosystem economics, market structure, user behavior, competitive dynamics, and where capital is flowing onchain.

And of course...agents 🦞. Our customers and users include Visa, Stripe, G-SIB Banks, Big 4 Accounting firms, BCG, Coinbase, Phantom, Uniswap and cited by the Federal Reserve.

Essence of the Role


Conduct regular outbound activities to key web3 prospects and inbound leads using platforms like Discord, Telegram, Twitter, LinkedIn, etc., to promote Allium.so’s data analytics solutions.

Meet with key stakeholders to understand prospective customers’ goals and assess how Allium.so can empower their web3 data needs.

Schedule and confirm new business discovery meetings after qualifying leads using the BANT methodology.

Collaborate closely with the revenue team to align on and execute Allium.so’s prospecting strategy.

Assist in crafting tailored messaging for outbound campaigns that highlight Allium.so’s value in blockchain analytics.

Communicate platform feedback and feature requests from prospects to Allium.so’s Product & Engineering teams to enhance our offerings.

Meet measurable activity targets consistently on a quarterly basis.

Utilize CRM and other tools daily to document leads, opportunities, and meetings effectively.

Forecast opportunity pipeline accurately and regularly to support Allium.so’s growth objectives.

What You'll Bring

Based in NYC

Strong willingness to attend events after working hours + travel for events

2+ years of experience prospecting in a sales role, ideally within software, infrastructure, or web3 industries.

Deep knowledge and enthusiasm for web3, blockchain, and data analytics, with an understanding of tools like Allium.so.

A track record of engaging and prospecting to senior stakeholders in the web3 ecosystem.

Willingness to navigate technical sales cycles and collaborate cross-functionally to deliver Allium.so’s complex data solutions.

Outstanding listening, verbal, and written communication skills to articulate Allium.so’s value proposition.

Proven success in consistently hitting measurable activity targets.

Ability to operate independently, in a high agency fashion

Don't take our word for it, what our customers say about us (https://www.allium.so/blog#love)

What some cool people have to say about us:

  • The Information's Top 50 Startups (https://www.allium.so/post/allium-named-to-the-informations-50-most-promising-startups-of-2025)

  • Mario Gabriele from The Generalist's Future 50 Startup List: https://www.allium.so/post/allium-named-awardee-of-the-generalists-inaugural-future-50-startups

  • Tomasz Tungus from Theory Ventures: https://tomtunguz.com/allium/

  • Bucky Moore from Kleiner Perkins: https://www.kleinerperkins.com/perspectives/allium-series-a/

Ok, now for some tough love. Here are the values we strive for at Allium:

  • Obsessiveness - The best people at Allium cannot put a problem down once they pick it up. We care more about the work than is strictly rational. Institutions trust us because our data is right. Right means caring about the small things. The decoded contract that ships with one wrong field. The label that is 99% accurate but wrong on the address that matters. The query that runs in 4 seconds when it should run in 400 milliseconds. Most companies tolerate these. We do not.

    Obsessiveness shows up as depth of care. It is not measured in hours worked or visible effort. You should feel something physical when work ships half-right. That instinct is what we hire for.

  • Pro Athlete Mindset - Consistency. Day in and day out, in pursuit of excellence. A win yesterday does not guarantee (or even imply!) a win tomorrow. I hope anyone who supports a failing sports team will feel the pain (cough Man United fans) of inconsistency

  • Figure It Out & Extreme Ownership - Every day is unexplored territory. There are new engineering frameworks, new legal docs, new compliance, new sales, new regulations, and new operational procedures every single day. If you don’t know it, learn it. If you can’t learn it, find someone or a product that does it. If you can’t find someone, find someone who can find someone. It is never a lack of resources, but lack of resourcefulness.

  • High Agency - (One of) the highest commonalities between all successful people is their responsiveness. Most successful billionaire CEOs still reply to emails within minutes (within working hours). And when you reply, respond fast with effective solutions - and even better, resolutions. If you’re looking for a superpower, you can’t go wrong with responsiveness. Well of course this doesn't make sense when you're an engineer coding in flow, but in general high agency of problem solving gets one very far in life

  • Leading from the Front - No one is going to listen (and adopt) your suggestion unless you lead by example. It’s one thing to say We need to do XYZ this better & it’s another thing to build an MVP and say “This is the way we should do things”. The proof of work and momentum goes a long way.

  • Strong Opinions On the Future (loosely held) - It is okay to be wrong, but what is not okay is not to have an idea of how a better future should be. Alliumites take pride in trying to improving everything about the company all the time.

  • Sense of (Allium) business smell - There are number of folks who live to eat at Allium, but the Allium smell we are talking about is that we love folks who naturally want to know why and how the work they are doing builds leverage for their teammates and also relates to the business goals

About the team

We invite people of all backgrounds (https://www.allium.so/about). We have engineers who learnt coding much later in life, who learnt coding on the side, we have engineers who are still in school and we also have engineers who went to the top schools (CMU, Stanford, UIUC, UPenn, Oxford, NUS, Cornell), all are welcome if one comes in with a curious mind and an infectious work ethic.

Administrative Benefits

  • Medical, Dental, Vision, Life and AD&D insurance - US folks get 100% coverage for Gold plans, 80% for dependents

  • Ownership - Meaningful early-stage equity. Every full-time employee receives a stock option grant so you can share directly in Allium's upside

  • Time off - Flexible, trust-based paid time off. We encourage people to take the rest they need. In every country we hire, our policies meet or exceed local statutory vacation requirements

  • Retirement - Company sponsored 401(k) plan in US so you can save pre-tax for the long term

All applicants have to answer this pop quiz: "What is an Allium? What is your favorite Allium?". Bonus points for the right pronunciation.
